lyrics:
[Intro: slow piano chords, soft kick and snap]

[Verse 1: tender male tenor, close]
I know you've got the drive ahead
I know the kids are waiting up
The nurse came by to dim the lights
I know I've said enough

[Pre-Chorus: organ under, voice lifting]
I'm not afraid, I'm not in pain
I just don't like the door

[Chorus: gospel choir joins, full and warm]
Sit with me a while
You don't have to talk
Sit with me a while
Let the clock just walk
I won't ask for more than this tonight
Sit with me a while

[Verse 2: voice softer, piano and bass]
Your mother used to do this, too
Just sit, and hum, and hold my sleeve
I never knew how much it was
Till there was no one who wouldn't leave

[Chorus: gospel choir, handclaps on the backbeat]
Sit with me a while
You don't have to talk
Sit with me a while
Let the clock just walk
I won't ask for more than this tonight
Sit with me a while

[Bridge: choir alone, humming, then one line]
Ten more minutes
Ten more minutes

[Final Chorus: choir highest, tenor ad-libbing above]
Sit with me a while
You don't have to talk
Sit with me a while
Let the clock just walk
I won't ask for more than this tonight
Sit with me a while

[Outro: piano, a chair pulled closer, a hand patted]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 84 BPM, 4/4, C major. Slow, swaying and churchy, a hymn with a backbeat.

VOICE: Male tenor, soft and vulnerable in the verses with a breathy falsetto on the high notes, fuller in the choruses. A gospel choir sings every chorus with him and hums the bridge. He ad-libs above them at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: Piano, a slow kick with a finger snap or soft snare, Hammond organ, a warm bass guitar, a gospel choir, handclaps, a small string section in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro piano. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:32 Pre-chorus. 0:42 Chorus 1. 1:06 Verse 2. 1:28 Chorus 2. 1:52 Bridge, choir humming. 2:06 Final chorus. 2:34 Outro, a chair and a patted hand, ends 2:56.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2014 gospel-pop: warm, dry and close, piano and voice in front, choir wide behind.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I just don't like the door' at 0:38.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man asking a stranger not to leave after one night. The same six words mean more from a father in a hospital bed to a son with his car keys in his hand.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Apologetic, honest, held, at ease.
